tasks.short: Answer employee questions, interpret agreements, and help management and employees resolve workplace problems.

steps.what: Receive questions and identify urgent, sensitive, or routine cases.
Find employee records, applicable contracts, policies, and previous correspondence.
Interpret relevant clauses and prepare a response or escalation.

loop.input: Employee question and authorised contract and policy passages, including versions and effective dates.
loop.output: Draft response with clause references, uncertainties, and suggested escalation.
loop.check: Verify references and dates mechanically; HR checks applicability and interpretation before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; missing, conflicting, or inapplicable sources return to HR.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed answers cover common questions; ambiguous questions and varied contract wording need contextual reading.

steps.what: Discuss the issue with employees and managers and hear their concerns.
Agree the resolution, responsibilities, or specialist escalation.
Record the outcome and assign follow-up reminders.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted case queue in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to records in the {HCM} and approved documents in the {DOCS}. Deterministic retrieval assembles the case file; a bounded answer desk drafts cited responses for HR approval. Approved action fields create follow-up tasks in the {PROJECT}, while employees retain direct access to HR conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies, contracts, and correspondence were scattered. Reliable interpretation still required someone who understood the employee's circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case routing can be configured, and coding assistance reduces the cost of connectors and source checks. Bounded drafting can handle varied wording without deciding the case.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, informal promises, source permissions, and relationship repair remain difficult. Contract interpretation still needs qualified review.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, notice unstated concerns, and negotiate a resolution that both sides can live with.

ambition.what: Preventive conflict consultations for team leads.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less document hunting and more early conversations. The manager can convene preventive consultations within existing delegation; employment decision rights do not expand.

reach.task: Prepare agreement interpretations for employee disputes.
reach.learn: Agreement hierarchy, clause applicability, and when to seek legal advice.

reach.task: Maintain case records and follow-up tasks.
reach.learn: Case taxonomy, restricted access, and retention rules.

evidence.claim: Restricted case routing, document retrieval, and approved-action reminders are feasible with configuration and deterministic integration.
IBM reported HR NPS of minus 35 in AskHR's first year after managers lost HR partners and the phone line; retain human access.

assumptions: Time shares are estimates for a typical mid-size company; substantial conversation time follows the supplied priors.
Retrieved records use existing permissions, lawful purposes, minimisation, and retention controls under GDPR.
The answer desk provides reviewed guidance and makes no significant employment decision; GDPR Article 22 remains relevant [S10].
National rules determine required employee consultation. Consultation and access effort is included; waiting can extend elapsed time.
Build ranges assume one initial case category and reuse of existing identity and document infrastructure.
unknowns: Which contracts, collective agreements, and policy versions apply.
Whether case handling already exists in the {HCM} or {HELPDESK}.
Actual question volume, sensitive-case proportion, and retrieval time.
Operating countries, consultation obligations, and approved record retention.
research_questions: What evidence measures clause accuracy and inappropriate escalation in reviewed HR answer desks?
Which national requirements govern this proposed employee-case processing?
new_work: Review draft interpretations and uncertain source matches.
Maintain approved policy versions and agreement applicability.
Handle cases that lack evidence or need specialist advice.
Check access logs and overdue follow-up exceptions.

tasks.short: Set priorities, allocate HR work, supervise staff, and coordinate delivery across HR services.

steps.what: Review recruitment, employee-case, pay-cycle, and project queues.
Compare deadlines and team availability in a capacity worksheet.
Agree priorities and resolve resource conflicts with the HR team.
Assign owners and due dates and explain expected outcomes.
Coach staff, review difficult cases, and remove delivery obstacles.
Request routine progress updates already available in team queues.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines queue totals from the {ATS}, {HCM}, {PAYROLL}, and {PROJECT} into a restricted {BI} workload view. Simple rules compare deadlines with declared team capacity, and configured task templates apply the manager's approved assignments in the {PROJECT}. Shared status removes duplicate progress requests; coaching and resource trade-offs stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Queues had different owners and status definitions. Maintaining a consolidated view cost more than checking systems and asking colleagues.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance makes small connectors and consistent status mappings cheaper to build. Existing task templates can handle assignments without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Case complexity is uneven, availability is imperfect, and urgent employee matters can disrupt plans. Capacity estimates cannot capture trust, experience, or emotional load.
tasks.human_edge: Balance urgency with staff development, recognise overload, and make defensible choices between competing HR needs.

ambition.what: Weekly allocation of HR capacity between urgent cases and improvement projects.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting status and more time coaching and rebalancing delivery. They can make weekly allocation decisions within the approved staffing budget; budget authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Schedule HR team development against service commitments.
reach.learn: Skill coverage, protected learning time, and capacity planning.

reach.task: Escalate pay-cycle dependencies before processing deadlines.
reach.learn: Cut-off calendars, dependency mapping, and exception severity.

evidence.claim: Queue aggregation, deadline comparisons, and task templates can use deterministic technology without model-generated staff rankings.
A Danish study across 11 occupations including HR reported 2.8% hours saved by chatbots; it does not establish HR-manager task savings.

assumptions: The capacity worksheet represents coordination across queues, not the primary record for every HR service.
Capacity uses declared availability and task estimates; it does not infer individual performance or rank staff.
National rules may require consultation for changes to staff-data processing or monitoring.
Model-based employee allocation or performance evaluation would require separate assessment under AI Act Annex III [S11]; this design uses human allocation decisions.
GDPR applies to identifiable workload information; viewers receive only the detail they need.
Build estimates cover an initial team and stable exports or APIs; elapsed consultation waits may be longer.
unknowns: Which HR queues are already consolidated in the {PROJECT}.
Whether staff maintain reliable task status and declared availability.
Available interfaces and permissions for pay-cycle status.
Current allocation authority, consultation arrangements, and escalation thresholds.
research_questions: Which workload measures predict HR service delays without turning into employee performance scoring?
What documented implementations measure the reduction in duplicate status requests?
new_work: Maintain status mappings and deadline calendars.
Correct stale task statuses and missing capacity entries.
Review delivery exceptions during weekly allocation.
Check that workload views do not expose restricted case details.

tasks.short: Handle staffing shortages, disputes, disciplinary cases, and dismissals through evidence, fair procedure, and difficult conversations.

steps.what: Receive the staffing problem and establish urgency and procedural route.
Gather relevant records and reconstruct events or staffing constraints.

loop.input: Selected case documents and correspondence with source identifiers.
loop.output: Draft chronology separating recorded events, allegations, and missing evidence.
loop.check: Validate source identifiers and dates; HR checks omissions, contradictions, and allegation labels.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; unresolved contradictions remain visible for human investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured records support direct assembly, but relevant events often appear in narrative correspondence.

steps.what: Hear employees and managers and test disputed facts or staffing needs.
Choose a proportionate staffing, mediation, disciplinary, or dismissal response.
Review procedure and approve the proposed employment action under delegated authority.
Prepare the action letter or written resolution from the approved decision.
Explain the decision, deliver written terms, and discuss practical next steps.
Update authorised records and initiate required staffing or exit follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure restricted case routes and procedural checklists in the {WORKFLOW}, with authorised evidence from the {HCM} and {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares a cited chronology, and deterministic templates prepare letters from approved decision fields. People investigate, decide, approve, and deliver employment actions; approved records trigger the appropriate follow-up in the {HCM} and {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was dispersed, procedures varied by case, and the consequences made broad automation unsuitable. Much of the work was already human judgement rather than administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations, chronology checks, and template generators are cheaper to build with coding assistance. Narrative extraction can assist preparation while leaving decisions with people.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, proportionality, legal procedure, staffing alternatives, and emotional consequences remain difficult. Unrecorded events cannot be reconstructed reliably by software.
tasks.human_edge: Hear conflicting accounts fairly, recognise power imbalances, and take responsibility for consequential decisions.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and paperwork leaves more time for interviews, mediation, and exploring staffing alternatives. Disciplinary and dismissal authority does not change.

reach.task: Check disciplinary procedure and advise on settlement options.
reach.learn: National procedure, collective agreements, proportionality, and evidence standards.

reach.task: Develop redeployment options for staffing shortages.
reach.learn: Skill matching, contractual constraints, and consultation requirements.

evidence.claim: Case checklists, approved-decision templates, and authorised record updates can use configuration and deterministic code.
Narrative chronology extraction needs review and does not establish truth, credibility, or an appropriate employment outcome.

assumptions: Cases branch by issue; mediation, disciplinary action, and dismissal are alternative routes rather than mandatory stages.
The chronology is an evidence-navigation aid and produces no credibility, performance, or dismissal score.
Significant employment decisions require meaningful human assessment under GDPR Article 22 where applicable [S10].
GDPR safeguards cover confidential records and any special-category data, including restricted access and lawful retention.
National rules and applicable agreements govern hearings, representation, consultation, and employment actions.
Consent and access ranges include applicable employee consultation; legal or consultation waiting can extend elapsed time.
Build estimates cover one procedural route before expansion.
unknowns: Applicable countries, agreements, and disciplinary procedures.
Who holds authority for each type of employment action.
Evidence quality, permitted data categories, and retention requirements.
How much time is currently spent on preparation versus conversations.
Whether action letters can use approved structured fields and existing templates.
research_questions: What documented evaluations test omissions and allegation handling in employment-case chronologies?
Which national procedural requirements must each proposed case route enforce?
new_work: Verify chronology completeness and distinguish allegations from established facts.
Maintain procedural routes and approved letter templates.
Handle missing evidence, disputed dates, and nonstandard decisions.
Audit that record updates follow the exact approved action and required delivery conditions.

tasks.short: Prepare evidence and represent the employer at personnel hearings and investigations.

steps.what: Receive the hearing notice and confirm deadlines, scope, and responsible people.
Select relevant employment records, correspondence, and signed decisions for the evidence bundle.
Prepare a chronology, issue summary, and references to supporting evidence.

loop.input: Selected evidence bundle and hearing scope, with immutable document identifiers.
loop.output: Draft chronology and issue summary with document and passage references.
loop.check: Check reference existence and dates; HR and counsel verify relevance, omissions, and factual wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unsupported claims are removed or marked unresolved for counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Indexing and pagination are deterministic, but narrative evidence needs contextual reading to draft an issue summary.

steps.what: Agree the organisational position, representation mandate, and limits on commitments.
Attend the hearing or investigation, answer questions, and respond within the mandate.
Review and approve any written submission and evidence disclosure.
Send the approved submission through the required channel and retain proof of delivery.
Record outcomes, deadlines, and owners for the required follow-up.

tasks.design: A restricted workspace in the {DOCS} uses deterministic collection, indexing, and pagination to assemble selected records from the {HCM} and {EMAIL}. A bounded loop drafts a cited hearing brief for HR and counsel review, while the {WORKFLOW} records mandates and disclosure approvals. People represent the employer and file approved submissions; structured follow-up fields create deadlines in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hearings were infrequent, evidence formats varied, and disclosure needed careful legal judgement. Building bespoke tooling was hard to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable case-file tools and cheaper custom code make indexing and deadline tracking practical. Bounded drafting can reduce reading effort without supplying legal strategy.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence relevance, privilege, permitted disclosure, witness credibility, and unexpected questions remain difficult. External submission channels and procedural requirements vary.
tasks.human_edge: Give credible testimony, respond under scrutiny, and exercise judgement within an agreed representation mandate.
tasks.altitude: Occasional hearing preparation takes less administrative time, leaving more time to test evidence and rehearse with counsel. Representation and settlement rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare hearing evidence and advise the employer's representative.
reach.learn: Evidence relevance, procedural deadlines, representation rights, and disclosure restrictions.

reach.task: Review the completeness and fairness of investigation records.
reach.learn: Discrimination indicators, balanced fact gathering, and protection against retaliation.

evidence.claim: Evidence indexing, pagination, provenance tracking, and deadline reminders can use deterministic technology.
Cited draft summaries can assist preparation, but this digest supplies no documented hearing-preparation deployment or measured saving.

assumptions: The sequence represents a hearing with a subsequent written submission; cases without one skip those stages.
The manager represents the employer only where permitted and within an approved mandate.
The model drafts from selected evidence and does not assess credibility, predict outcomes, or devise legal strategy.
GDPR applies to evidence processing and disclosure, including special-category data where present.
National rules determine representation, procedural deadlines, preservation, and employee consultation requirements.
Submission by {EMAIL} is a typical route; mandated portals or physical filings require adaptation.
Build estimates assume reuse of case-file infrastructure. Consultation and external-access waiting can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Hearing types, jurisdictions, and rules on who may represent the employer.
Whether counsel approval is required for each disclosure or commitment.
Evidence locations, preservation requirements, and privilege restrictions.
Actual hearing frequency and preparation effort.
Required submission channels, authentication, and delivery-proof standards.
research_questions: What documented evaluations measure omitted or unsupported claims in employment-hearing summaries?
Which procedural rules govern evidence handling and representation in the relevant national forum?
new_work: Verify summaries against original evidence and check omitted context.
Maintain bundle templates, source references, and preservation controls.
Review disclosure scope and remove material outside the approved submission.
Confirm receipt and convert agreed obligations into structured follow-up fields.

role.altitude: The HR manager spends less time finding records, consolidating status, and preparing paperwork. More time goes to coaching, preventive conflict consultations, and careful case decisions; employment and representation authority remain subject to existing delegation.
reach: Labor Relations Specialist: agreement interpretation, fair procedure, and hearing preparation.
Training and Development Manager: protect staff development while maintaining HR service capacity.
Human Resources Specialist: develop practical staffing and redeployment alternatives.
Equal Opportunity Representative: assess fairness and completeness in investigation records.
skills_to_grow: Check source-grounded drafts and distinguish allegations from established facts.
Use workload data to prioritise services without treating it as a staff ranking.
Design case routes, approval conditions, and exception handling.
Apply GDPR safeguards and recognise when national consultation rules apply.
Develop mediation, coaching, and evidence-based interviewing skills.
role.ambitious_version: Offer preventive conflict consultations and make weekly HR capacity decisions from reliable service data. Keep direct human access and reserve consequential employment decisions for accountable people.
